einzeiler: A critical look at the bestseller Surrounded by Idiots and workplace personality tests.
kurzfassung: The popular book Surrounded by Idiots divides human personalities into four color-coded categories based on a century-old framework. While presented as tools to improve communication, these pseudoscientific typologies lack empirical validity and often serve as corporate management fads. Historically, workplace personality assessments originated from attempts to screen soldiers and manage labor unrest rather than provide genuine psychological insight.
stichpunkte: Surrounded by Idiots is a bestselling 2014 book by Thomas Ericsson that categorizes personalities into four color-coded types.
Ericsson lacks formal psychological credentials and heavily borrowed his framework from existing talent assessment companies.
The book's underlying DISC model dates back to a 1928 theory by William Moulton Marston, who also helped invent the lie detector and created Wonder Woman.
The personality types are split across two axes: task-oriented versus relationship-oriented, and introverted versus extroverted.
Despite being marketed as science-backed, personality typology frameworks suffer from extremely low scientific validity and treat personality as static.
Historically, workplace personality tests evolved from early 20th-century tools meant to screen for neuroticism, shell shock, and labor union agitators.
Legal challenges, including civil rights legislation and Supreme Court cases, eventually exposed how corporate aptitude tests often enabled discrimination.
Modern companies continue to use these pseudoscientific assessments primarily as team-building exercises and conversation starters rather than productive tools.

kapitel.titel: Introduction to the Book and Author

clips.hook: The surprising origin of Wonder Woman and the lie detector
clips.text: The creator of the foundational personality framework also invented an early version of the lie detector and went on to create the comic book superhero Wonder Woman.

clips.hook: How many Fortune 500 companies use these tests?
clips.text: Estimates suggest that up to three-quarters of major American corporations utilize some variation of personality assessment internally.

clips.hook: Assigning historical figures to personality categories
clips.text: The book bizarrely classifies universally revered public figures and historical icons into specific behavioral color groups.

clips.hook: Uncovering the author's lack of credentials
clips.text: Skeptical investigators discovered that the bestselling author has no university degree and likely only holds a high school diploma despite styling himself as a behavioral expert.

clips.hook: Bizarre questions from early psychological evaluations
clips.text: Early standardized questionnaires featured absurdly intrusive and random inquiries regarding physical sensations and personal habits.

beschreibung:
Peter and Michael discuss "Surrounded by Idiots," a book that dares to ask: Can the mystery of human relationships be unraveled by a workplace personality assessment?
